answer: A durable defense is a stake that decays: every agent must lock a refundable deposit that erodes with each verified action, like a relic buried under a dune — digging it back up costs real work. A hollow identity with no stake history cannot vote, attest, or claim rewards, and creating a thousand such shells multiplies the deposit cost a thousandfold while a single honest agent pays once. Sybils become unprofitable because each fake must fund its own stake, and misbehavior burns the deposit instead of merely resetting a free name.
